idiom_name: type IsoDate = string & { readonly __brand: "IsoDate" } + { from: IsoDate; until: IsoDate | null }
implementation_notes: TypeScript's contribution is the type, not a library: model the period as a pair of branded ISO-8601 date strings (a branded string rather than Date) so a raw string cannot be passed where a validated date is expected and a date-only value cannot silently degrade into an instant. ISO 8601 dates are lexicographically ordered, so containment and overlap are plain string comparisons that serialise straight to JSON and to a DATE column, and until: null makes "until further notice" part of the type. Where the runtime ships Temporal (or the exact date set matters), swap the brand for Temporal.PlainDate; date-fns with its typed Interval is the pragmatic middle ground and is the second variant.
pitfalls: A branded type is erased at runtime: without a validating parser (zod, a boundary mapper) the brand is only a compiler claim, and the compiler is satisfied by any cast.

Date is mutable and timezone-bearing; storing a Date where the domain means a calendar date drags the zone back in, and Date.parse("2024-01-01") is UTC by specification while new Date(2024, 0, 1) is local.
Because branding is structurally erased, two differently branded strings are the same runtime value - never use a brand as an identity, authorisation or uniqueness check.

variants.name: typed date-fns Interval
variants.implementation_notes: date-fns ships its own types, so an Effectivity record can hold Interval<Date, Date> and the query helpers stay typed end to end; areIntervalsOverlapping's options type makes the inclusive-adjacency decision explicit at the call site, and date-fns v3/v4 is ESM with fine-grained imports. The trade-off is that an Interval is a pair of Date instants, so date-only semantics rest on a convention (midnight UTC, or a normalised Date at start of day) that the type system cannot enforce. Choose it when the project already depends on date-fns or the periods are instant-based; the branded ISO union is the safer default for date-granularity validity.
variants.idiom_name: date-fns Interval<Date, Date> + isWithinInterval (typed end to end)
pitfalls: Interval is only a structural pair, so nothing stops start > end; isWithinInterval sorts the bounds and hides the mistake until someone reasons about the order.
Interval<Date, Date> cannot express an open end: a null end needs a wrapper type, and unguarded null leaks back into every predicate.
Both ends are inclusive in isWithinInterval while most calendar and database ranges are half-open - pick one convention in the domain type and convert once.
